mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops > 0.5% in 1 month and SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for three consecutive months and SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops > 1% in 1 month and SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy in low-growth environment
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and GDPC1 YoY < 2% and SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a robust labor market, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE drops > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE drops > 0.3% in 1 month and SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters and SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
